answer:
Let \(A,B,C,D,E,F\) denote Ada, Ben, Cam, Dee, Eli, Finn. Since every player has degree \(2\), every connected component of the game graph must be a cycle. With six vertices, the only possible component decompositions are:

- one \(6\)-cycle; or
- two \(3\)-cycles.

Ada already has degree \(2\) via \(AB,AC\), and Finn cannot play Ada. The possible sets of Finn’s opponents are therefore all \(2\)-subsets of \(\{B,C,D,E\}\), except \(\{B,C\}\).

\[
\boxed{
\{B,D\},\ \{B,E\},\ \{C,D\},\ \{C,E\},\ \{D,E\}
}
\]

Here are supporting completions:

| Finn’s opponents | Full edge set | Components |
|---|---|---|
| \(\{B,D\}\) | \(AB, AC, DE, BF, DF, CE\) | one \(6\)-cycle \(A-B-F-D-E-C-A\) |
| \(\{B,E\}\) | \(AB, AC, DE, BF, EF, CD\) | one \(6\)-cycle \(A-B-F-E-D-C-A\) |
| \(\{C,D\}\) | \(AB, AC, DE, CF, DF, BE\) | one \(6\)-cycle \(A-C-F-D-E-B-A\) |
| \(\{C,E\}\) | \(AB, AC, DE, CF, EF, BD\) | one \(6\)-cycle \(A-C-F-E-D-B-A\) |
| \(\{D,E\}\) | \(AB, AC, DE, DF, EF, BC\) | two \(3\)-cycles: \(A-B-C-A\) and \(D-E-F-D\) |

The remaining possibility, Finn playing \(\{B,C\}\), is impossible: then Ben and Cam already have degree \(2\), leaving Dee and Eli each needing one more opponent, but their only remaining possible edge would be \(DE\), which has already been played and cannot be repeated.

Thus the game graph can have either a single \(6\)-cycle component or two triangle components, and Finn’s possible opponent sets are exactly
\[
\boxed{\{Ben,Dee\},\{Ben,Eli\},\{Cam,Dee\},\{Cam,Eli\},\{Dee,Eli\}.}
\]
